finalCandidate.hypothesis: Longer trend age and a deeper but still bounded pullback may improve entry location when volatility is elevated.
finalCandidate.marketMechanism: A deeper liquidity sweep that holds structure can reset extension without invalidating the trend.
finalCandidate.expectedRegime: BULL with elevated but non-spiking volatility
finalCandidate.entryLogic: Deeper pullback, structure hold, bullish close and no late chase.
finalCandidate.invalidationLogic: Structure breaks or price remains below EMA after the pullback.
finalCandidate.expectedFailureMode: Trend age becomes exhaustion rather than continuation.

candidate.hypothesis: A compressed range followed by a volume-confirmed breakout and a shallow retest can preserve continuation edge without late chasing.
candidate.marketMechanism: Order-flow imbalance from a range expansion is tested when former resistance becomes support.
candidate.expectedRegime: BULL with BTC/ETH agreement and non-extreme breadth
candidate.entryLogic: Prior-bar clean high breakout, current-bar retest of the former high, close back above the level, controlled extension.
candidate.invalidationLogic: Retest closes below former resistance or stop is hit before target.
candidate.expectedFailureMode: Failed breakout, thin volume, or entry after an already extended impulse.

candidate.hypothesis: A stricter breakout volume threshold should separate clean continuation from noisy range breaks.
candidate.marketMechanism: High participation confirms a state change before the support retest.
candidate.entryLogic: Thirty-bar level break, high relative volume, shallow retest and reclaim without extension above one ATR.
candidate.invalidationLogic: Level rejection or a wide retest that signals distribution.
candidate.expectedFailureMode: Volume spike without follow-through or broad market disagreement.

candidate.hypothesis: A longer compression and a conservative retest can reduce false breakouts even at the cost of fewer trades.
candidate.marketMechanism: Energy accumulation in a narrow range creates asymmetric continuation only after the level is defended.
candidate.entryLogic: Twenty-bar break after compression, retest within one ATR, positive momentum re-acceleration.
candidate.invalidationLogic: Retest fails or the signal is too far from EMA/level.
candidate.expectedFailureMode: Compression resolves in the opposite direction or lacks breadth support.

candidate.hypothesis: A mature higher-timeframe uptrend should reward controlled pullbacks that re-accelerate from EMA/structure.
candidate.marketMechanism: Continuation buyers defend a known value area after weak counter-trend supply is absorbed.
candidate.entryLogic: Bull trend age, one-to-four ATR pullback, close above EMA with positive momentum acceleration.
candidate.invalidationLogic: Trend alignment breaks or the pullback exceeds the structural risk band.
candidate.expectedFailureMode: Trend exhaustion and a deeper regime transition masked as a pullback.

candidate.hypothesis: Shallower pullbacks with a stronger momentum turn may avoid buying exhausted rebounds.
candidate.marketMechanism: Fast re-acceleration after a shallow reset indicates demand remains dominant.
candidate.entryLogic: Short controlled pullback, RSI recovery, volume expansion and limited EMA distance.
candidate.invalidationLogic: No momentum turn or close under the fast EMA.

candidate.hypothesis: Longer trend age and a deeper but still bounded pullback may improve entry location when volatility is elevated.
candidate.marketMechanism: A deeper liquidity sweep that holds structure can reset extension without invalidating the trend.
candidate.expectedRegime: BULL with elevated but non-spiking volatility
candidate.entryLogic: Deeper pullback, structure hold, bullish close and no late chase.
candidate.invalidationLogic: Structure breaks or price remains below EMA after the pullback.
candidate.expectedFailureMode: Trend age becomes exhaustion rather than continuation.

candidate.hypothesis: A measured volatility expansion from compression can create directional continuation before the move becomes crowded.
candidate.marketMechanism: Volatility re-pricing plus volume participation produces a temporary directional imbalance.
candidate.entryLogic: Compression, range expansion, volume confirmation, close near high and controlled extension.
candidate.invalidationLogic: Expansion lacks follow-through or is an isolated spike.

candidate.hypothesis: A stricter compression and expansion threshold should reject single-bar anomalies.
candidate.marketMechanism: Sustained range expansion with two-sided confirmation is more likely to represent information arrival.
candidate.entryLogic: Tight compression, current and prior expansion confirmation, high volume and positive benchmark alignment.
candidate.invalidationLogic: One-bar spike, weak close, or extension beyond one ATR.
candidate.expectedFailureMode: Breakout occurs after the exploitable move has already happened.

candidate.hypothesis: A lower threshold variant tests whether the structural idea survives realistic signal sparsity without a narrow optimum.
candidate.marketMechanism: Early but confirmed expansion may retain more of the move than late breakout entry.
candidate.entryLogic: Compression followed by positive expansion, moderate participation and no extreme extension.
candidate.invalidationLogic: Expansion fails to hold the compression boundary.
candidate.expectedFailureMode: False positive expansion in a range.
